on.s: Hvernig skal Heimdall kenna? Svá, at kalla hann son níu mæðra eða vörð goða, svá sem fyrr er ritat, eða hvíta ás, Loka dólg mensækir Freyju. Heimdallar höfuð heitir sverð. Svá er sagt, at hann var lostinn mannshöfði í gegnum. Um þat er kveðit í Heimdallar galdri, ok er síðan kallat höfuð mjötuðr Heimdallar. Sverð heitir manns mjötuðr. Heimdallr er eigandi Gulltopps. Hann er ok tilsækir Vágaskers ok Singasteins. Þá deilði hann við Loka um Brísingamen. Hann heitir ok Vindlér. Úlfr Uggason kvað í Húsdrápu langa stund eftir þeiri frásögu, ok er þess þar getit, at þeir váru í selalíkjum. Hann er ok sonr Óðins.

is.s: Hvernig skal Heimdall kenna? Svo, að kalla hann son níu mæðra eða vörð goða, svo sem fyrr er ritað, eða hvíta ás, Loka dólg mensækir Freyju. Heimdallar höfuð heitir sverð. Svo er sagt, að hann var lostinn mannshöfði í gegnum. Um það er kveðið í Heimdallar galdri, og er síðan kallað höfuð mjötuður Heimdallar. Sverð heitir manns mjötuður. Heimdallur er eigandi Gulltopps. Hann er og tilsækir Vágaskers og Singasteins. Þá deildi hann við Loka um brísingamen. Hann heitir og Vindlér. Úlfur Uggason kvað í Húsdrápu langa stund eftir þeirri frásögu, og er þess þar getið, að þeir voru í selalíkjum. Hann er og sonur Óðins.

en.s: "How should one periphrase Heimdallr? By calling him Son of Nine Mothers, or Watchman of the Gods, as already has been written; or White God, Foe of Loki, Seeker of Freyja's Necklace. A sword is called Heimdallr's Head: for it is said that he was pierced by a man's head. The tale thereof is told in Heimdalar-galdr; and ever since a head is called Heimdallr's Measure; a sword is called Man's Measure. Heimdallr is the Possessor of Gulltoppr; he is also Frequenter of Vágasker and Singasteinn, where he contended with Loki for the Necklace Brísinga-men, he is also called Vindlér. Úlfr Uggason composed a long passage in the Húsdrápa on that legend, and there it is written that they were in the form of seals. Heimdallr also is son of Odin.

en-modern.s: "How should one periphrase Heimdallr? By calling him Son of Nine Mothers, or Watchman of the Gods, as has already been written; or White God, Foe of Loki, Seeker of Freyja's Necklace. A sword is called Heimdallr's Head, for it is said that he was pierced by a man's head. The story is told in Heimdalar-galdr; and ever since a head has been called Heimdallr's Measure, and a sword is called Man's Measure. Heimdallr is the Possessor of Gulltoppr; he is also Frequenter of Vágasker and Singasteinn, where he fought with Loki for the necklace Brísinga-men. He is also called Vindlér. Úlfr Uggason composed a long passage in the Húsdrápa on that legend, and it is recorded there that they were in the form of seals. Heimdallr is also a son of Odin.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna Tý? Svá, at kalla hann einhenda ás ok úlfs fóstra, víga guð, son Óðins.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna Tý? Svo, að kalla hann einhenda ás og úlfs fóstra, víga guð, son Óðins.

en.s: "How should one periphrase Týr? By calling him the One-handed God, and Fosterer of the Wolf, God of Battles, Son of Odin.

en-modern.s: "How should one periphrase Týr? By calling him the One-handed God, and Fosterer of the Wolf, God of Battles, Son of Odin.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna Braga? Svá, at kalla hann Iðunnar ver, frumsmið bragar ok inn síðskeggja ás - af hans nafni er sá kallaðr skeggbragi, er mikit skegg hefir - ok sonr Óðins.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna Braga? Svo, að kalla hann Iðunnar ver, frumsmið bragar og hinn síðskeggja ás - af hans nafni er sá kallaður skeggbragi, er mikið skegg hefur - og sonur Óðins.

en.s: "How should one periphrase Bragi? By calling him Husband of Idunn, First Maker of Poetry, and the Long-bearded God (after his name, a man who has a great beard is called Beard-Bragi) and Son of Odin.

en-modern.s: "How should one periphrase Bragi? By calling him Husband of Idunn, First Maker of Poetry, and the Long-bearded God (after his name, a man with a great beard is called Beard-Bragi) and Son of Odin.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna Víðar? Hann má kalla inn þögla ás, eiganda járnskós, dólg ok bana Fenrisúlfs, hefniás goðanna, byggviás föðurtófta ok son Óðins, bróður ásanna.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna Víðar? Hann má kalla hinn þögla ás, eiganda járnskós, dólg og bana Fenrisúlfs, hefniás goðanna, byggviás föðurtófta og son Óðins, bróður ásanna.

en.s: "How should one periphrase Vídarr? He maybe called the Silent God, Possessor of the Iron Shoe, Foe and Slayer of Fenris-Wolf, Avenger of the Gods, Divine Dweller in the Homesteads of the Fathers, Son of Odin, and Brother of the Æsir.

en-modern.s: "How should one periphrase Vídarr? He may be called the Silent God, Possessor of the Iron Shoe, Foe and Slayer of Fenris-Wolf, Avenger of the Gods, Divine Dweller in the Homesteads of the Fathers, Son of Odin, and Brother of the Æsir.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna Vála? Svá, at kalla hann son Óðins ok Rindar, stjúpson Friggjar, bróður ásanna, hefniás Baldrs, dólg Haðar ok bana hans, byggvanda föðurtófta.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna Vála? Svo, að kalla hann son Óðins og Rindar, stjúpson Friggjar, bróður ásanna, hefniás Baldurs, dólg Haðar og bana hans, byggvanda föðurtófta.

en.s: "How should Váli be periphrased? Thus: by calling him Son of Odin and Rindr, Stepson of Frigg, Brother of the Æsir, Baldr's Avenger, Foe and Slayer of Hödr, Dweller in the Homesteads of the Fathers.

en-modern.s: "How should Váli be periphrased? By calling him Son of Odin and Rindr, Stepson of Frigg, Brother of the Æsir, Baldr's Avenger, Foe and Slayer of Hödr, Dweller in the Homesteads of the Fathers.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna Höð? Svá, at kalla hann blinda ás, Baldrs bana, skjótanda Mistilteins, son Óðins, Heljar sinna, Vála dólg.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna Höð? Svo, að kalla hann blinda ás, Baldurs bana, skjótanda Mistilteins, son Óðins, Heljar sinna, Vála dólg.

en.s: "How should one periphrase Hödr? Thus: by calling him the Blind God, Baldr's Slayer, Thrower of the Mistletoe, Son of Odin, Companion of Hel, Foe of Váli.

en-modern.s: "How should one periphrase Hödr? By calling him the Blind God, Baldr's Slayer, Thrower of the Mistletoe, Son of Odin, Companion of Hel, Foe of Váli.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna Ull? Svá, at kalla hann son Sifjar, stjúp Þórs, öndurás, bogaás, veiðiás, skjaldarás.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna Ull? Svo, að kalla hann son Sifjar, stjúp Þórs, öndurás, bogaás, veiðiás, skjaldarás.

en.s: How should Ullr be periphrased? By calling him Son of Sif, Stepson of Thor, God of the Snowshoe, God of the Bow, Hunting-God, God of the Shield.

en-modern.s: How should Ullr be periphrased? By calling him Son of Sif, Stepson of Thor, God of the Snowshoe, God of the Bow, Hunting-God, God of the Shield.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna Hæni? Svá, at kalla hann sessa eða sinna eða mála Óðins ok inn skjóta ás ok inn langa fót ok aurkonung.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna Hæni? Svo, að kalla hann sessa eða sinna eða mála Óðins og hinn skjóta ás og hinn langa fót og aurkonung.

en.s: How should Hœnir be periphrased? By calling him Bench-Mate or Companion or Friend of Odin, the Swift of God, the Long-Footed, and' King of Clay.⟦1⟧

en-modern.s: How should Hœnir be periphrased? By calling him Bench-Mate or Companion or Friend of Odin, the Swift God, the Long-Footed, and King of Clay.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna Loka? Svá, at kalla hann son Fárbauta ok Laufeyjar, Nálar, bróður Býleists ok Helblinda, föður Vánargands, þat er Fenrisúlfr, ok Jörmundgands, þat er Miðgarðsormr, ok Heljar ok Nara ok Ála, frænda ok föðurbróður, vársinna ok sessa Óðins ok ása, heimsæki ok kistuskrúð Geirröðar, þjóf jötna, hafrs ok Brísingamens ok Iðunnar epla, Sleipnis frænda, ver Sigynjar, goða dólgr, hárskaði Sifjar, bölvasmiðr, inn slægi áss, rægjandi ok vélandi goðanna, ráðbani Baldrs, inn bundni áss, þrætudólgr Heimdallar ok Skaða. Svá sem hér segir Úlfr Uggason:

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna Loka? Svo, að kalla hann son Fárbauta og Laufeyjar, Nálar, bróður Býleists og Helblinda, föður Vánargands, það er Fenrisúlfur, og Jörmundgands, það er Miðgarðsormur, og Heljar og Nara og Ála, frænda og föðurbróður, vársinna og sessa Óðins og ása, heimsæki og kistuskrúð Geirröðar, þjóf jötna, hafrs og Brísingamens og Iðunnar epla, Sleipnis frænda, ver Sigynjar, goða dólgur, hárskaði Sifjar, bölvasmiður, hinn slægi ás, rægjandi og vélandi goðanna, ráðbani Baldurs, hinn bundni ás, þrætudólgur Heimdallar og Skaða. Svo sem hér segir Úlfur Uggason:

en.s: "How should one periphrase Loki? Thus: call him Son of Fárbauti and Laufey, or of Nil, Brother of Býleistr and of Helblindi, Father of the Monster of Ván (that is, Fenris-Wolf), and of the Vast Monster (that is, the Midgard Serpent), and of Hel, and Nari, and Áli; Kinsman and Uncle, Evil Companion and Bench-Mate of Odin and the Æsir, Visitor and Chest-Trapping of Geirrödr, Thief of the Giants, of the Goat, of Brísinga-men, and of Idunn's Apples, Kinsman of Sleipnir, Husband of Sigyn, Foe of the Gods, Harmer of Sif's Hair, Forger of Evil, the Sly God, Slanderer and Cheat of the Gods, Contriver of Baldr's Death, the Bound God, Wrangling Foe of Heimdallr and of Skadi. Even as Úlfr Uggason sings here:

en-modern.s: "How should one periphrase Loki? Call him Son of Fárbauti and Laufey, or of Nál, Brother of Býleistr and of Helblindi, Father of the Monster of Ván (that is, Fenris-Wolf), and of the Vast Monster (that is, the Midgard Serpent), and of Hel, and Nari, and Áli; Kinsman and Uncle, Evil Companion and Bench-Mate of Odin and the Æsir, Visitor and Chest-Ornament of Geirrödr, Thief of the Giants, of the Goat, of Brísinga-men, and of Idunn's Apples, Kinsman of Sleipnir, Husband of Sigyn, Foe of the Gods, Harmer of Sif's Hair, Forger of Evil, the Sly God, Slanderer and Cheat of the Gods, Contriver of Baldr's Death, the Bound God, Wrangling Foe of Heimdallr and of Skadi. As Úlfr Uggason sings here:

l: The son of mothers eight and one,
I make known songs of praise.
The famed defender of the rainbow,
the son of eight mothers and one,
I make known songs of praise.

on.s: Hér er þess getit, að Heimdallr er son níu mæðra.

is.s: Hér er þess getið, að Heimdallur er son níu mæðra.

en.s: Here it is written that Heimdallr is the son of nine mothers.

en-modern.s: Here it is recorded that Heimdallr is the son of nine mothers.

on.s: Nú skal enn segja dæmi, af hverju þær kenningar eru, er nú váru ritaðar, er áðr váru eigi dæmi til sögð, svá sem Bragi sagði Ægi, at Þórr var farinn í austrvega at berja troll, en Óðinn reið Sleipni í Jötunheima ok kom til þess jötuns, er Hrungnir hét. Þá spyrr Hrungnir, hvat manna sá er með gullhjálminn, er ríðr loft ok lög, ok segir, at hann á furðugóðan hest. Óðinn sagði, at þar vill hann veðja fyrir höfði sínu, at engi hestr skal vera jafngóðr í Jötunheimum. Hrungnir segir, at sá er góðr hestr, en hafa lézt hann mundu miklu stórfetaðra hest. Sá heitir Gullfaxi. Hrungnir varð reiðr ok hleypr upp á hest sinn ok hleypir eftir honum ok hyggr at launa honum ofrmæli. Óðinn hleypir svá mikit, at hann var á öðru leiti fyrir, en Hrungnir hafði svá mikinn jötunmóð, at hann fann eigi fyrr en hann kom inn of ásgrindr.

is.s: Nú skal enn segja dæmi, af hverju þær kenningar eru, er nú voru ritaðar, er áður voru eigi dæmi til sögð, svo sem Bragi sagði Ægi, að Þór var farinn í austrvega að berja troll, en Óðinn reið Sleipni í Jötunheima og kom til þess jötuns, er Hrungnir hét. Þá spyr Hrungnir, hvað manna sá er með gullhjálminn, er ríður loft og lög, og segir, að hann á furðugóðan hest. Óðinn sagði, að þar vill hann veðja fyrir höfði sínu, að enginn hestur skal vera jafngóður í Jötunheimum. Hrungnir segir, að sá er góður hestur, en hafa lést hann myndu miklu stórfetaðra hest. Sá heitir Gullfaxi. Hrungnir varð reiður og hleypur upp á hest sinn og hleypir eftir honum og hyggur að launa honum ofrmæli. Óðinn hleypir svo mikið, að hann var á öðru leiti fyrir, en Hrungnir hafði svo mikinn jötunmóð, að hann fann eigi fyrr en hann kom hinn of ásgrindur.

en.s: "Now an account shall be given of the source of those metaphors which have but now been recorded, and of which no accounts were rendered before: even such as Bragi gave to Ægir, telling how Thor had gone into the east to slay trolls, and Odin rode Sleipnir into Jötunheim and visited that giant who was named Hrungnir. Hrungnir asked what manner of man he with the golden helm might be, who rode through air and water; and said that the stranger had a wondrous good steed. Odin said he would wager his head there was no horse in Jötunheim that would prove equally good. Hrungnir answered that it was a good horse, but declared that he had a much better paced horse which was called Gold-Mane. Hrungnir had become angry, and vaulted up onto his horse and galloped after him, thinking to pay him for his boasting. Odin gal loped so furiously that he was on the top of the next hill first; but Hrungnir was so filled with the giant's frenzy that he took no heed until he had come in beyond the gates of Ásgard.

en-modern.s: "Now an account shall be given of where those metaphors come from which have just been recorded, and which have not been explained before: such as the one Bragi gave to Ægir, telling how Thor had gone into the east to kill trolls, and Odin rode Sleipnir into Jötunheim and visited the giant called Hrungnir. Hrungnir asked what sort of man this was in the golden helmet, who rode through air and water, and said that the stranger had a wonderfully good horse. Odin said he would wager his head that there was no horse in Jötunheim that would prove as good. Hrungnir answered that it was a good horse, but declared that he had a horse with a much better stride, called Gold-Mane. Hrungnir had grown angry; he leapt onto his horse and galloped after him, meaning to pay him back for his boasting. Odin galloped so hard that he was on the top of the next hill first; but Hrungnir was so filled with a giant's fury that he noticed nothing until he had come in through the gates of Ásgard.

on.s: Ok er hann kom at hallardurum, buðu æsir honum til drykkju. Hann gekk í höllina ok bað fá sér at drekka. Váru þá teknar þær skálir, er Þórr var vanr at drekka af, ok snerti Hrungnir ór hverri. En er hann gerðist drukkinn, þá skorti eigi stór orð. Hann lézt skyldu taka upp Valhöll ok færa í Jötunheima, en sökkva Ásgarði, en drepa goð öll, nema Freyju ok Sif vill hann heim hafa með sér, en Freyja ein þorir þá at skenkja honum, ok drekka lézt hann mundu allt ásaöl.

is.s: Og er hann kom að hallardurunum, buðu æsir honum til drykkju. Hann gekk í höllina og bað fá sér að drekka. Voru þá teknar þær skálir, er Þór var vanur að drekka af, og snerti Hrungnir úr hverri. En er hann gerðist drukkinn, þá skorti eigi stór orð. Hann lést skyldu taka upp Valhöll og færa í Jötunheima, en sökkva Ásgarði, en drepa guð öll, nema Freyju og Sif vill hann heim hafa með sér, en Freyja ein þorir þá að skenkja honum, og drekka lést hann myndu allt ásaöl.

en.s: When he came to the hall-door, the Æsir invited him to drink. He went within and ordered drink to be brought to him, and then those flagons were brought in from which Thor was wont to drink; and Hrungnir swilled from each in turn. But when he had become drunken, then big words were not wanting: he boasted that he would lift up Valhall and carry it to Jötunheim, and sink Ásgard and kill all the gods, save that he would take Freyja and Sif home with him. Freyja alone dared pour for him; and he vowed that he would drink all the ale of the Æsir.

en-modern.s: When he came to the door of the hall, the Æsir invited him to drink. He went inside and called for drink to be brought to him, and the flagons that Thor usually drank from were brought in; Hrungnir gulped from each in turn. But once he had become drunk there was no shortage of big words: he boasted that he would lift up Valhall and carry it to Jötunheim, sink Ásgard and kill all the gods, except that he would take Freyja and Sif home with him. Freyja alone dared to pour for him, and he swore that he would drink all the ale of the Æsir.

on.s: En er ásum leiddust ofryrði hans, þá nefna þeir Þór. Því næst kom Þórr í höllina ok hafði á lofti hamarinn ok var allreiðr ok spyrr, hverr því ræðr, er jötnar hundvísir skulu þar drekka, eða hverr seldi Hrungni grið at vera í Valhöll eða hví Freyja skal skenkja honum sem at gildi ása.

is.s: En er ásum leiddust ofryrði hans, þá nefna þeir Þór. Því næst kom Þór í höllina og hafði á lofti hamarinn og var allreiður og spyr, hver því ræður, er jötnar hundvísir skulu þar drekka, eða hver seldi Hrungni grið að vera í Valhöll eða hví Freyja skal skenkja honum sem að gildi ása.

en.s: But when his overbearing insolence became tiresome to the Æsir, they called on the name of Thor.

"Straightway Thor came into the hall, brandishing his hammer, and he was very wroth, and asked who had advised that these dogs of giants be permitted to drink there, or who had granted Hrungnir safe-conduct to be in Valhall, or why Freyja should pour for him as at a feast of the Æsir.

en-modern.s: But when the Æsir grew tired of his overbearing insolence, they called on the name of Thor.

"At once Thor came into the hall, brandishing his hammer. He was very angry, and asked who had decided that these dogs of giants should be allowed to drink there, who had granted Hrungnir safe-conduct to be in Valhall, and why Freyja should pour for him as at a feast of the Æsir.

on.s: Þá svarar Hrungnir ok sér ekki vinaraugum til Þórs, sagði, at Óðinn bauð honum til drykkju ok hann var á hans griðum. Þá mælti Þórr, at þess boðs skal Hrungnir iðrast, áðr hann komi út.

is.s: Þá svarar Hrungnir og sér ekki vinaraugum til Þórs, sagði, að Óðinn bauð honum til drykkju og hann var á hans griðum. Þá mælti Þór, að þess boðs skal Hrungnir iðrast, áður hann komi út.

en.s: Then Hrungnir answered, looking at Thor with no friendly eyes, and said that Odin had invited him to drink, and he was under his safe-conduct. Thor declared that Hrungnir should repent of that invitation before he got away.

en-modern.s: Then Hrungnir answered, giving Thor no friendly look, and said that Odin had invited him to drink and that he was under his safe-conduct. Thor declared that Hrungnir would regret that invitation before he got away.

on.s: Hrungnir segir, at Ása-Þór er þat lítill frami at drepa hann vápnlausan. Hitt er meiri hugraun, ef hann þorir at berjast við hann at landamæri á Grjóttúnagörðum, - "ok hefir þat verit mikit fólskuverk," sagði hann, "er ek lét eftir heima skjöld minn ok hein. En ef ek hefða hér vápn mín, þá skyldum vit nú reyna hólmgönguna, en at öðrum kosti legg ek þér við níðingsskap, ef þú vill drepa mik vápnlausan."

is.s: Hrungnir segir, að Ása-Þór er það lítill frami að drepa hann vápnlausan. Hitt er meiri hugraun, ef hann þorir að berjast við hann að landamæri á Grjóttúnagörðum, - "og hefur það verið mikið fólskuverk," sagði hann, "er eg lét eftir heima skjöld minn og hein. En ef eg hefði hér vopn mín, þá skyldum vit nú reyna hólmgönguna, en að öðrum kosti legg eg þér við níðingsskap, ef þú vill drepa mig vápnlausan."

en.s: Hrungnir answered that Ása-Thor would have scant renown for killing him, weaponless as he was: it were a greater trial of his courage if he dared fight with Hrungnir on the border at Grjótúnagard. 'And it was a great folly,' said he, 'when I left my shield and hone behind at home; if I had my weapons here, then we should try single-combat. But as matters stand, I declare thee a coward if thou wilt slay me, a weaponless man.'

en-modern.s: Hrungnir answered that Ása-Thor would win little glory by killing him, unarmed as he was: it would be a greater test of his courage if he dared to fight Hrungnir on the border at Grjótúnagard. 'And it was very foolish of me,' he said, 'to leave my shield and whetstone behind at home; if I had my weapons here, we would try single combat. But as things stand, I declare you a coward if you kill me, an unarmed man.'

on.s: Þórr vill fyrir engan mun bila at koma til einvígis, er honum var hólmr skoraðr, því at engi hafði honum þat fyrr veitt. Fór þá Hrungnir braut leið sína ok hleypði ákafliga, þar til er hann kom í Jötunheima, ok varð ferð hans allfræg með jötnum ok þat, at stefnulag var komit á með þeim Þór. Þóttust jötnar hafa mikit í ábyrgð, hvárr sigr fengi. Þeim var ills ván af Þór, ef Hrungnir léti, fyrir því at hann var þeira sterkastr.

is.s: Þór vill fyrir engan mun bila að koma til einvígis, er honum var hólmur skoraður, því að enginn hafði honum það fyrr veitt. Fór þá Hrungnir braut leið sína og hleypti ákaflega, þar til er hann kom í Jötunheima, og varð ferð hans allfræg með jötnum og það, að stefnulag var komið á með þeim Þór. Þóttust jötnar hafa mikið í ábyrgð, hvor sigur fengi. Þeim var ills von af Þór, ef Hrungnir léti, fyrir því að hann var þeirra sterkastur.

en.s: Thor was by no means anxious to avoid the fight when challenged to the field, for no one had ever offered him single-combat before.

"Then Hrungnir went his way, and galloped furiously until he came to Jötunheim. The news of his journey was spread abroad among the giants, and it became noised abroad that a meeting had been arranged between him and Thor; the giants deemed that they had much at stake, who should win the victory, since they looked for ill at Thor's hands if Hrungnir perished, he being strongest of them all.

en-modern.s: Thor was by no means anxious to avoid the fight when challenged to the field, for no one had ever offered him single combat before.

"Then Hrungnir went on his way, and galloped hard until he came to Jötunheim. The news of his journey spread among the giants, and word got about that a meeting had been arranged between him and Thor. The giants felt that they had a great deal at stake in who won the victory, since they expected the worst from Thor if Hrungnir was killed, he being the strongest of them all.

on.s: Þá gerðu jötnar mann á Grjóttúnagörðum af leiri, ok var hann níu rasta hár, en þriggja breiðr undir hönd, en ekki fengu þeir hjarta svá mikit, at honum sómði, fyrr en þeir tóku úr meri nökkurri, ok varð honum þar eigi stöðugt, þá er Þórr kom.

is.s: Þá gerðu jötnar mann á Grjóttúnagörðum af leiri, og var hann níu rasta hár, en þriggja breiður undir hönd, en ekki fengu þeir hjarta svo mikið, að honum sómði, fyrr en þeir tóku úr meri nokkurri, og varð honum þar eigi stöðugt, þá er Þór kom.

en.s: Then the giants made a man of clay at Grjótúnagard: he was nine miles high and three broad under the arm-pits; but they could get no heart big enough to fit him, until they took one from a mare. Even that was not steadfast within him, when Thor came.

en-modern.s: Then the giants made a man of clay at Grjótúnagard: he was nine miles high and three broad under the armpits. But they could find no heart big enough to fit him until they took one from a mare. Even that did not hold steady inside him when Thor came.

on.s: Hrungnir átti hjarta þat, er frægt er, af hörðum steini ok tindótt með þrimr hornum, svá sem síðan er gert ristubragð þar, er Hrungnishjarta heitir. Af steini var ok höfuð hans. Skjöldr hans var ok steinn, víðr ok þjokkr, ok hafði hann skjöldinn fyrir sér, er hann stóð á Grjóttatúnagörðum ok beið Þórs, en hein hafði hann fyrir vápn ok reiddi of öxl ok var ekki dælligr. Á aðra hlið honum stóð leirjötunninn, er nefndr er Mökkurkálfi, ok var hann allhræddr. Svá er sagt, at hann meig, er hann sá Þór.

is.s: Hrungnir átti hjarta það, er frægt er, af hörðum steini og tindótt með þrem hornum, svo sem síðan er gert ristubragð þar, er Hrungnishjarta heitir. Af steini var og höfuð hans. Skjöldur hans var og steinn, víður og þjokkur, og hafði hann skjöldinn fyrir sér, er hann stóð á Grjóttatúnagörðum og beið Þórs, en hein hafði hann fyrir vopn og reiddi of öxl og var ekki dælligur. Á aðra hlið honum stóð leirjötunninn, er nefndur er Mökkurkálfi, og var hann allhræddur. Svo er sagt, að hann meig, er hann sá Þór.

en.s: Hrungnir had the heart which is notorious, of hard stone and spiked with three corners, even as the written character is since formed, which men call Hrungnir's Heart. His head also was of stone; his shield too was stone, wide and thick, and he had the shield before him when he stood at Grjótúnagard and waited for Thor. Moreover he had a hone for a weapon, and brandished it over his shoulders, and he was not a pretty sight. At one side of him stood the clay giant, which was called Mökkurkálfi: he was sore afraid, and it is said that he wet himself when he saw Thor.

en-modern.s: Hrungnir had the heart that is famous: of hard stone, and pointed with three corners, like the written character made since then which is called Hrungnir's Heart. His head was also of stone; his shield was stone too, wide and thick, and he held the shield in front of him as he stood at Grjótúnagard and waited for Thor. He also had a whetstone for a weapon, and brandished it over his shoulders, and he was not a pretty sight. On one side of him stood the clay giant, who was called Mökkurkálfi: he was terribly afraid, and it is said that he wet himself when he saw Thor.

on.s: Þórr fór til hólmstefnu ok með honum Þjálfi.

is.s: Þór fór til hólmstefnu og með honum Þjálfi.

en.s: "Thor went to the meeting-place, and Thjálfi with him.

en-modern.s: "Thor went to the meeting place, and Thjálfi with him.

on.s: Þá rann Þjálfi fram at, þar er Hrungnir stóð, ok mælti til hans: "Þú stendr óvarliga, jötunn, hefir skjöldinn fyrir þér, en Þórr hefir sét þik, ok ferr hann it neðra í jörðu, ok mun hann koma neðan at þér."

is.s: Þá rann Þjálfi fram að, þar er Hrungnir stóð, og mælti til hans: "Þú stendur óvarlega, jötunn, hefur skjöldinn fyrir þér, en Þór hefur séð þig, og fer hann it neðri í jörðu, og mun hann koma neðan að þér."

en.s: Then Thjálfi ran forward to the spot where Hrungnir stood and said to him: 'Thou standest unwarily, Giant, having the shield before thee: for Thor has seen thee, and comes hither down below the earth, and will come at thee from beneath.'

en-modern.s: Then Thjálfi ran forward to where Hrungnir stood and said to him: 'You are standing carelessly, giant, with your shield in front of you: Thor has seen you, and he is coming here down under the earth, and will come at you from below.'

on.s: Þá skaut Hrungnir skildinum undir fætr sér ok stóð á, en tvíhendi heinina. Því næst sá hann eldingar ok heyrði þrumur stórar. Sá hann þá Þór í ásmóði. Fór hann ákafliga ok reiddi hamarinn ok kastaði um langa leið at Hrungni. Hrungnir færir upp heinina báðum höndum ok kastar í mót. Mætir hon hamrinum á flugi, ok brotnar sundr heinin. Fellr annarr hlutr á jörð, ok eru þar af orðin öll heinberg. Annarr hlutr brast í höfði Þór, svá at hann fell fram á jörð. En hamarrinn Mjöllnir kom í mitt höfuð Hrungni ok lamði hausinn í smán mola, ok fell hann fram yfir Þór, svá at fótr hans lá of háls Þór. En Þjálfi vá at Mökkurkálfa, ok fell hann við lítinn orðstír.

is.s: Þá skaut Hrungnir skildinum undir fætur sér og stóð á, en tvíhendi heinina. Því næst sá hann eldingar og heyrði þrumur stórar. Sá hann þá Þór í ásmóði. Fór hann ákaflega og reiddi hamarinn og kastaði um langa leið að Hrungni. Hrungnir færir upp heinina báðum höndum og kastar í mót. Mætir hún hamrinum á flugi, og brotnar sundur heinin. Fellur annar hlutur á jörð, og eru þar af orðin öll heinberg. Annar hlutur brast í höfði Þór, svo að hann féll fram á jörð. En hamarinn Mjöllnir kom í mitt höfuð Hrungni og lamði hausinn í smáan mola, og féll hann fram yfir Þór, svo að fótur hans lá of háls Þór. En Þjálfi vá að Mökkurkálfa, og féll hann við lítinn orðstír.

en.s: Then Hrungnir thrust the shield under his feet and stood upon it, wielding the hone with both hands. Then speedily he saw lightnings and heard great claps of thunder; then he saw Thor in God-like anger, who came forward furiously and swung the hammer and cast it at Hrungnir from afar off. Hrungnir lifted up the hone in both hands and cast it against him; it struck the hammer in flight, and the hone burst in sunder: one part fell to the earth, and thence are come all the flint-rocks; the other burst on Thor's head, so that he fell forward to the earth. But the hammer Mjöllnir struck Hrungnir in the middle of the head, and smashed his skull into small crumbs, and he fell forward upon Thor, so that his foot lay over Thor's neck. Thjálfi struck at Mökkurkálfi, and he fell with little glory.

en-modern.s: Then Hrungnir pushed the shield under his feet and stood on it, gripping the whetstone with both hands. Very soon he saw lightning and heard great claps of thunder; then he saw Thor in his godlike anger, who came on furiously, swung the hammer and threw it at Hrungnir from a long way off. Hrungnir lifted the whetstone in both hands and threw it against him. It struck the hammer in flight and the whetstone broke apart: one part fell to the ground, and from it come all the flint rocks; the other smashed into Thor's head, so that he fell forward to the ground. But the hammer Mjöllnir struck Hrungnir in the middle of the head and smashed his skull into small crumbs, and he fell forward over Thor, so that his foot lay across Thor's neck. Thjálfi attacked Mökkurkálfi, and he fell with little glory.

on.s: Þá gekk Þjálfi til Þórs ok skyldi taka fót Hrungnis af honum ok gat hvergi valdit. Þá gengu til æsir allir, er þeir spurðu at Þórr var fallinn, ok skyldu taka fótinn af honum ok fengu hvergi komit.

is.s: Þá gekk Þjálfi til Þórs og skyldi taka fót Hrungnis af honum og gat hvergi valdið. Þá gengu til æsir allir, er þeir spurðu að Þór var fallinn, og skyldu taka fótinn af honum og fengu hvergi komið.

en.s: Thereupon Thjálfi went over to Thor and would have lifted Hrungnir's foot off him, but could not find sufficient strength. Straightway all the Æsir came up, when they, learned that Thor was fallen, and would have lifted the foot from off him, and could do nothing.

en-modern.s: Then Thjálfi went over to Thor and tried to lift Hrungnir's foot off him, but did not have the strength. At once all the Æsir came up, when they learned that Thor had fallen, and tried to lift the foot off him, and could do nothing.

on.s: Þá kom til Magni, sonr Þórs ok Járnsöxu. Hann var þá þrínættr. Hann kastaði fæti Hrungnis af Þór ok mælti: "Sé þar ljótan harm, faðir, er ek kom svá síð. Ek hygg, at jötun þenna myndak hafa lostit í hel með hnefa mínum, ef ek hefða fundit hann."

is.s: Þá kom til Magni, sonur Þórs og Járnsöxu. Hann var þá þrínættur. Hann kastaði fæti Hrungnis af Þór og mælti: "Sé þar ljótan harm, faðir, er eg kom svo síðan. Eg hygg, að jötun þennan mundak hafa lostið í hel með hnefa mínum, ef eg hefði fundið hann."

en.s: Then Magni came up, son of Thor and Járnsaxa: he was then three nights old; he cast the foot of Hrungnir off Thor, and spake: 'See how ill it is, father, that I came so late: I had struck this giant dead with my fist, methinks, if I had met with him.'

en-modern.s: Then Magni came up, the son of Thor and Járnsaxa. He was three nights old at the time. He threw Hrungnir's foot off Thor and said: 'See what a pity it is, father, that I came so late: I think I would have struck this giant dead with my fist if I had met him.'

on.s: Þá stóð Þórr upp ok fagnaði vel syni sínum ok sagði, at hann myndi verða mikill fyrir sér, - "ok vil ek," sagði hann, "gefa þér hestinn Gullfaxa, er Hrungnir hefir átt."

is.s: Þá stóð Þór upp og fagnaði vel syni sínum og sagði, að hann myndi verða mikill fyrir sér, - "og vil eg," sagði hann, "gefa þér hestinn Gullfaxa, er Hrungnir hefur átt."

en.s: Thor arose and welcomed his son, saying that he should surely become great; 'And I will give thee,' he said, the horse Gold-Mane, which Hrungnir possessed.'

en-modern.s: Thor got up and welcomed his son, saying that he would surely grow to be great. 'And I will give you,' he said, 'the horse Gold-Mane, which Hrungnir owned.'

on.s: Þá mælti Óðinn ok sagði, at Þórr gerði rangt, er hann gaf þann inn góða hest gýgjarsyni, en eigi föður sínum.

is.s: Þá mælti Óðinn og sagði, að Þór gerði rangt, er hann gaf þann hinn góða hest gýgjarsuni, en eigi föður sínum.

en.s: Then Odin spake and said that Thor did wrong to give the good horse to the son of a giantess, and not to his father.

en-modern.s: Then Odin spoke and said that Thor did wrong to give that good horse to the son of a giantess, and not to his father.

on.s: Þórr fór heim til Þrúðvanga, ok stóð heinin í höfði honum. Þá kom til völva sú, er Gróa hét, kona Aurvandils ins frækna. Hon gól galdra sína yfir Þór, til þess er heinin losnaði. En er Þórr fann þat ok þótti þá ván, at braut myndi ná heininni, þá vildi hann launa Gró lækninguna ok gera hana fegna, sagði henni þau tíðendi, at hann hafði vaðit norðan yfir Élivága ok hafði borit í meis á baki sér Aurvandil norðan ór Jötunheimum, ok þat til jartegna, at ein tá hans hafði staðit ór meisinum, ok var sú frerin, svá at Þórr braut af ok kastaði upp á himin ok gerði af stjörnu þá, er heitir Aurvandilstá. Þórr sagði, at eigi myndi langt til, at Aurvandill myndi heim koma, en Gróa varð svá fegin, at hon mundi enga galdra, ok varð heinin eigi lausari ok stendr enn í höfði Þór, ok er þat boðit til varnanar at kasta hein of gólf þvert, því at þá hrærist heinin í höfði Þór. Eftir þessi sögu hefir ort Þjóðólfr hvinverski í Haustlöng."   Þá mælti Ægir: "Mikill þótti mér Hrungnir fyrir sér. Vann Þórr meira þrekvirki nökkut, þá er hann átti við troll?"

is.s: Þór fór heim til Þrúðvanga, og stóð heinin í höfði honum. Þá kom til völva sú, er Gróa hét, kona Aurvandils hins frækna. Hún gól galdra sína yfir Þór, til þess er heinin losnaði. En er Þór fann það og þótti þá von, að braut myndi ná heininni, þá vildi hann launa Gró lækninguna og gera hana fegna, sagði henni þau tíðindi, að hann hafði vaðið norðan yfir Élivága og hafði borið í meis á baki sér Aurvandil norðan úr Jötunheimum, og það til jartegna, að ein tá hans hafði staðið úr meisinum, og var sú frerin, svo að Þór braut af og kastaði upp á himin og gerði af stjörnu þá, er heitir Aurvandilstá. Þór sagði, að eigi myndi langt til, að Aurvandill myndi heim koma, en Gróa varð svo fegin, að hún myndi enga galdra, og varð heinin eigi lausari og stendur enn í höfði Þór, og er það boðið til varnanar að kasta hein of gólf þvert, því að þá hrærist heinin í höfði Þór. Eftir þessi sögu hefur ort Þjóðólfur hvinverski í Haustlöng."   Þá mælti Ægir: "Mikill þótti mér Hrungnir fyrir sér. Vann Þór meira þrekvirki nokkurt, þá er hann átti við troll?"

en.s: "Thor went home to Thrúdvangar, and the hone remained sticking in his head. Then came the wise woman who was called Gróa, wife of Aurvandill the Valiant: she sang her spells over Thor until the hone was loosened. But when Thor knew that, and thought that there was hope that the hone might be removed, he desired to reward Gróa for her leech-craft and make her glad, and told her these things: that he had waded from the north over Icy Stream and had borne Aurvandill in a basket on his back from the north out of Jötunheim. And he added for a token, that one of Aurvandill's toes had stuck out of the basket, and became frozen; wherefore Thor broke it off and cast it up into the heavens, and made thereof the star called Aurvandill's Toe. Thor said that it would not be long ere Aurvandill came home: but Gróa was so rejoiced that she forgot her incantations, and the hone was not loosened, and stands yet in Thor's head. Therefore it is forbidden to cast a hone across the floor, for then the hone is stirred in Thor's head. Thjódólfr of Hvin has made a song after this tale in the Haustlöng. [It says there:

l: On the high and painted surface
Of the hollow shield, still further
One may see how the Giant's Terror
The angry son of Jörd drove
To the play of steel; below him
In the heart of Meili's Brother.
All the bright gods' high mansions
With hail the earth was beaten
Along his course, when the he-goats
Drew the god of the smooth wain forward
The Earth, the Spouse of Odin,
With the bitter foe of earth-folk.
Rocks shook, and crags were shivered;
And give way fast before him,
That was the wise gods' mandate,
By the Friend of the snout-troll's crusher.
The fiend of the roaring mountain;
Of Earth's Son, that the whetter
In the skull of Odin's offspring,

en-modern.s: "Thor went home to Thrúdvangar, and the whetstone stayed stuck in his head. Then the wise woman called Gróa came, the wife of Aurvandill the Valiant. She sang her spells over Thor until the whetstone began to come loose. When Thor noticed that, and thought there was hope that the whetstone might be removed, he wanted to reward Gróa for her healing and make her glad, and told her this news: that he had waded from the north over Icy Stream and had carried Aurvandill in a basket on his back, from the north out of Jötunheim. And as proof he added that one of Aurvandill's toes had stuck out of the basket and frozen, so Thor broke it off and threw it up into the sky, and made from it the star called Aurvandill's Toe. Thor said that it would not be long before Aurvandill came home. But Gróa was so overjoyed that she forgot her spells, and the whetstone came no looser, and it is still in Thor's head. That is why it is forbidden to throw a whetstone across the floor, for then the whetstone in Thor's head is stirred. Thjódólfr of Hvin has composed a poem on this story in the Haustlöng. [It says there:

and give way fast before him,
that was the wise gods' command,
did not wait long after that
by the Friend of the snout-troll's crusher.
the fiend of the roaring mountain;
when the Breaker of the Hill-Danes
of Earth's Son, so that the whetter
in the skull of Odin's offspring,
with stories, I had from Thórleifr."]

on.s: Þá svarar Bragi: "Mikillar frásagnar er þat vert, er Þórr fór til Geirröðargarða. Þá hafði hann eigi hamarinn Mjöllni eða megingjarðar eða járngreipr, ok olli því Loki. Hann fór með honum, því ar Loka hafði þat hent, þá er hann flaug einu sinni at skemmta sér með valsham Friggjar, at hann flaug fyrir forvitni sakar í Geirröðargarða ok sá þar höll mikla, settist ok sá inn of glugg. En Geirröðr leit í móti honum ok mælti, at taka skyldi fuglinn ok færa honum, en sendimaðr komst nauðuliga á hallarvegginn, svá var hann hár. Þat þótti Loka gott, er hann sótti erfiðliga til hans, ok ætlaði sér stund at fljúga eigi upp, fyrr en hann hafði farit allt torleiðit. En er maðrinn sótti at honum, þá beinir hann fluginn ok spyrnir við fast, ok eru þá fætrnir fastir. Var Loki tekinn þar höndum ok færðr Geirröði jötni. En er hann sá augu hans, þá grunaði hann, at maðr myndi vera, ok bað hann svara, en Loki þagði. Þá læsti Geirröðr Loka í kistu ok svelti hann þar þrjá mánuðr. En þá er Geirröðr tók hann upp ok beiddi hann orða, þá sagði Loki, hverr hann var, ok til fjörlausnar vann hann Geirröði þess eiða, at hann skyldi koma Þór í Geirröðargarða, svá at hann hefði hvárki hamarinn né megingjarðar.

is.s: Þá svarar Bragi: "Mikillar frásagnar er það vert, er Þór fór til Geirröðargarða. Þá hafði hann eigi hamarinn Mjöllni eða Megingjarðir eða járngreipur, og olli því Loki. Hann fór með honum, því ar Loka hafði það hent, þá er hann flaug einu sinni að skemmta sér með valsham Friggjar, að hann flaug fyrir forvitni sakir í Geirröðargarða og sá þar höll mikla, settist og sá hinn of glugg. En Geirröður leit í móti honum og mælti, að taka skyldi fuglinn og færa honum, en sendimaður komst nauðulega á hallarvegginn, svo var hann hár. Það þótti Loka gott, er hann sótti erfiðlega til hans, og ætlaði sér stund að fljúga eigi upp, fyrr en hann hafði farið allt torleiðið. En er maðurinn sótti að honum, þá beinir hann fluginn og spyrnir við fast, og eru þá fætrnir fastir. Var Loki tekinn þar höndum og færður Geirröði jötni. En er hann sá augu hans, þá grunar hann, að maður myndi vera, og bað hann svara, en Loki þagði. Þá læsti Geirröður Loka í kistu og svelti hann þar þrjá mánuður. En þá er Geirröður tók hann upp og beiddi hann orða, þá sagði Loki, hver hann var, og til fjörlausnar vann hann Geirröði þess eiða, að hann skyldi koma Þór í Geirröðargarða, svo að hann hefði hvárki hamarinn né Megingjarðir.

en.s: Then said, Ægir: "Methinks Hrungnir was of great might. Did Thor accomplish yet more valorous deeds when he had to do with the trolls?" And Bragi answered: "It is worthy to be told at length, how Thor went to Geirrödr's dwelling. At that time he had not the hammer Mjöllnir with him, nor his Girdle of Might, nor the iron gauntlets: and that was the fault of Loki, who went with him. For once, flying in his sport with Frigg's hawk-plumage, it had happened to Loki to fly for curiosity's sake into Geirrödr's court. There he saw a great hall, and alighted and looked in through the window; and Geirrödr looked up and saw him, and commanded that the bird be taken and brought to him, But he who was sent could scarce get to the top of the wall, so high was it; and it seemed pleasant to Loki to see the man striving with toil and pains to reach him, and he thought it was not yet time to fly away until the other had accomplished the perilous climb. When the man pressed hard after him, then he stretched his wings for flight, and thrust out vehemently, but now his feet were stuck fast.

So Loki was taken and brought before Geirrödr the giant; but when Geirrödr saw his eyes, he suspected that this might be a man, and bade him answer; but Loki was silent. Then Geirrödr shut Loki into a chest and starved him there three months. And now when Geirrödr took him out and commanded him to speak, Loki told who he was; and by way of ransom for his life he swore to Geirrödr with oaths that he would get Thor to come into Geirrödr's dwelling in such a fashion that he should have neither hammer nor Girdle of Might with him.

en-modern.s: Then Ægir said: "Hrungnir seems to me to have been very mighty. Did Thor do even braver deeds when he had dealings with the trolls?" And Bragi answered: "The story of how Thor went to Geirrödr's dwelling deserves to be told at length. At that time he did not have the hammer Mjöllnir with him, nor his Girdle of Might, nor the iron gauntlets, and that was the fault of Loki, who went with him. For once, when Loki was flying for amusement in Frigg's hawk-plumage, it happened that out of curiosity he flew into Geirrödr's court. There he saw a great hall, and he alighted and looked in through the window. Geirrödr looked up and saw him, and ordered the bird to be caught and brought to him. But the man who was sent could hardly get to the top of the wall, it was so high. Loki enjoyed seeing the man struggle so hard to reach him, and he decided not to fly away until the man had finished the dangerous climb. When the man was almost upon him, he spread his wings to fly and pushed off hard, but now his feet were stuck fast.

So Loki was caught and brought before the giant Geirrödr. When Geirrödr saw his eyes, he suspected that this might be a man, and told him to answer; but Loki was silent. Then Geirrödr shut Loki in a chest and starved him there for three months. When Geirrödr took him out and ordered him to speak, Loki said who he was; and to ransom his life he swore oaths to Geirrödr that he would get Thor to come to Geirrödr's dwelling with neither his hammer nor his Girdle of Might.

on.s: Þórr kom til gistingar til gýgjar þeirar, er Gríðr er kölluð. Hon var móðir Víðars ins þögla. Hon sagði Þór satt frá Geirröði, at hann var jötunn hundvíss ok illr viðreignar. Hon léði honum megingjarða ok járngreipr, er hon átti, ok staf sinn, er heitir Gríðarvölr.

is.s: Þór kom til gistingar til gýgjar þeirrar, er Gríður er kölluð. Hún var móðir Víðars hins þögla. Hún sagði Þór satt frá Geirröði, að hann var jötunn hundvíss og illur viðreignar. Hún léði honum megingjarða og járngreipur, er hún átti, og staf sinn, er heitir Gríðarvölur.

en.s: "Thor came to spend the night with that giantess who was called Grídr, mother of Vídarr the Silent. She told Thor the truth concerning Geirrödr, that he was a crafty giant and ill to deal with; and she lent him the Girdle of Might and iron gloves which she possessed, and her staff also, which was called Grídr's Rod.

en-modern.s: "Thor came to spend the night with the giantess called Grídr, the mother of Vídarr the Silent. She told Thor the truth about Geirrödr: that he was a cunning giant and hard to deal with. She lent him the Girdle of Might and the iron gloves that she owned, and also her staff, which was called Grídr's Rod.

on.s: Þá fór Þórr til ár þeirar, er Vimur heitir, allra á mest. Þá spennti hann sik megingjörðum ok studdi forstreymis Gríðarvöl, en Loki helt undir megingjarðar. Ok þá er Þórr kom á miðja ána, þá óx svá mjök áin, at uppi braut á öxl honum. Þá kvað Þórr þetta:

is.s: Þá fór Þór til ár þeirrar, er Vimur heitir, allra á mest. Þá spennti hann sig megingjörðum og studdi forstreymis Gríðarvöl, en Loki hélt undir Megingjarðir. Og þá er Þór kom á miðja ána, þá óx svo mjög áin, að uppi braut á öxl honum. Þá kvað Þór þetta:

en.s: Then Thor proceeded to the river named Vimur, greatest of all rivers. There he girded himself with the Girdle of Might and braced firmly downstream with Grídr's Rod, and Loki held on behind by the Girdle of Might. When Thor came to mid-current, the river waxed so greatly that it broke high upon his shoulders. Then Thor sang this:

en-modern.s: Then Thor went on to the river called Vimur, the greatest of all rivers. There he fastened the Girdle of Might around him and braced himself firmly against the current with Grídr's Rod, while Loki held on behind by the Girdle of Might. When Thor reached the middle of the stream, the river rose so much that it broke high on his shoulders. Then Thor sang this:

on.s: 65 Vax-at-tu nú, Vimur, alls mik þik vaða tíðir jötna garða í; veiztu, ef þú, vex, at þá vex mér ásmegin jafnhátt upp sem himinn.

on.s: Þá sér Þórr uppi í gljúfrum nökkurum, at Gjálp, dóttir Geirröðar stóð þar tveim megin árinnar, ok gerði hon árvöxtinn.

is.s: Þá sér Þór uppi í gljúfrum nokkrum, að Gjálp, dóttir Geirröðar stóð þar tveim megin árinnar, og gerði hún árvöxtinn.

en.s: "Then Thor saw Gjálp, daughter of Geirrödr, standing in certain ravines, one leg in each, spanning the river, and she was causing the spate.

en-modern.s: "Then Thor saw Gjálp, Geirrödr's daughter, standing in a ravine astride the river, with one leg on each side, and she was causing the flood.

on.s: Þá tók Þórr upp ór ánni stein mikinn ok kastaði at henni ok mælti svá: "At ósi skal á stemma."

is.s: Þá tók Þór upp úr ánni stein mikinn og kastaði að henni og mælti svo: "Að ósi skal á stemma."

en.s: Then Thor snatched up a great stone out of the river and cast it at her, saying these words: 'At its source should a river be stemmed.'

en-modern.s: Then Thor snatched a great stone out of the river and threw it at her, saying: 'A river should be dammed at its source.'

on.s: Eigi missti hann, þar er hann kastaði til. Ok í því bili bar hann at landi ok fekk tekit reynirunn nökkurn ok steig svá ór ánni. Því er það orðtak haft, at reynir er björg Þórs.

is.s: Eigi missti hann, þar er hann kastaði til. Og í því bili bar hann að landi og fékk tekið reynirunn nokkurn og steig svo úr ánni. Því er það orðtak haft, að reynir er björg Þórs.

en.s: Nor did he miss that at which he threw. In that moment he came to the shore and took hold of a rowan-clump, and so climbed out of the river; whence comes the saying that rowan is Thor's deliverance.

en-modern.s: And he did not miss what he threw at. At that moment he reached the bank, caught hold of a clump of rowan and so climbed out of the river; and that is the origin of the saying that the rowan is Thor's rescue.

on.s: En er Þórr kom til Geirröðar, þá var þeim félögum vísat fyrst í geitahús til herbergis, ok var þar einn stóll til sætis, ok sat Þórr þar. Þá varð hann þess varr, at stóllinn fór undir honum upp at ræfri. Hann stakk Gríðarveli upp í raftana ok lét sígast fast á stólinn. Varð þá brestr mikill, ok fylgði skrækr. Þar höfðu verit undir stólinum dætr Geirröðar, Gjálp ok Greip, ok hafði hann brotit hrygginn í báðum.

is.s: En er Þór kom til Geirröðar, þá var þeim félögum vísað fyrst í geitahús til herbergis, og var þar einn stóll til sætis, og sat Þór þar. Þá varð hann þess var, að stóllinn fór undir honum upp að ræfri. Hann stakk Gríðarveli upp í raftana og lét sígast fast á stólinn. Varð þá brestur mikill, og fylgdi skrækur. Þar höfðu verið undir stólinum dætur Geirröðar, Gjálp og Greip, og hafði hann brotið hrygginn í báðum.

en.s: "Now when Thor came before Geirrödr, the companions were shown first into the goat-fold⟦1⟧ for their entertainment, and there was one chair there for a seat, and Thor sat there. Then he became aware that the chair moved under him up toward the roof: he thrust Grídr's Rod up against the rafters and pushed back hard against the chair. Then there was a great crash, and screaming followed. Under the chair had been Geirrödr's daughters, Gjálp and Greip; and he had broken both their backs.

en-modern.s: "When Thor came to Geirrödr, he and his companion were first shown into the goat-shed as their lodging. There was one chair there to sit on, and Thor sat on it. Then he noticed that the chair was moving under him, up towards the roof. He thrust Grídr's Rod up against the rafters and pushed down hard on the chair. There was a great crash, followed by screaming. Under the chair had been Geirrödr's daughters, Gjálp and Greip, and he had broken both their backs.

on.s: Þá lét Geirröðr kalla Þór í höllina til leika. Þar váru eldar stórir eftir endilangri höll. En er Þórr kom gagnvart Geirröði, þá tók Geirröðr með töng járnsíu glóandi ok kastar at Þór, en Þórr tók í móti með járngreipum ok færir á loft síuna, en Geirröðr hljóp undir járnsúlu at forða sér. Þórr kastaði síunni ok laust gegnum súluna ok gegnum Geirröð ok gegnum vegginn ok svá fyrir útan í jörðina."

is.s: Þá lét Geirröður kalla Þór í höllina til leika. Þar voru eldar stórir eftir endilangri höll. En er Þór kom gagnvart Geirröði, þá tók Geirröður með töng járnsíu glóandi og kastar að Þór, en Þór tók í móti með járngreipum og færir á loft síuna, en Geirröður hljóp undir járnsúlu að forða sér. Þór kastaði síunni og laust gegnum súluna og gegnum Geirröð og gegnum vegginn og svo fyrir utan í jörðina."

en.s: Then Geirrödr had Thor called into the hall to play games. There were great fires the whole length of the hall. When Thor came up over against Geirrödr, then Geirrödr took up a glowing bar of iron with the tongs and cast it at Thor. Thor caught it with his iron gloves and raised the bar in the air, but Geirrödr leapt behind an iron pillar to save himself. Thor lifted up the bar and threw it, and it passed through the pillar and through Geirrödr and through the wall, and so on out, even into the earth.

en-modern.s: Then Geirrödr had Thor called into the hall to play games. There were great fires along the whole length of the hall. When Thor came up opposite Geirrödr, Geirrödr picked up a glowing bar of iron with the tongs and threw it at Thor. Thor caught it with his iron gloves and raised the bar in the air, but Geirrödr leapt behind an iron pillar to save himself. Thor lifted the bar and threw it, and it went through the pillar and through Geirrödr and through the wall, and so on outside into the earth.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna Frigg? Svá, at kalla hana dóttur Fjörgyns, kona Óðins, móður Baldrs, elju Jarðar ok Rindar ok Gunnlaðar ok Gerðar, sværa Nönnu, dróttning ása ok ásynja, Fullu ok valshams ok Fensala.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna Frigg? Svo, að kalla hana dóttur Fjörgyns, kona Óðins, móður Baldurs, elju Jarðar og Rindar og Gunnlaðar og Gerðar, sværa Nönnu, dróttning ása og ásynja, Fullu og valshams og Fensala.

en.s: How should one periphrase Frigg? Call her Daughter of Fjörgynn, Wife of Odin, Mother of Baldr, Co-Wife of Jörd and Rindr and Gunnlöd and Grídr, Mother-in-law of Nanna, Lady of the Æsir and Ásynjur, Mistress of Fulla and of the Hawk-Plumage and of Fensalir.

en-modern.s: How should one periphrase Frigg? Call her Daughter of Fjörgynn, Wife of Odin, Mother of Baldr, Co-Wife of Jörd and Rindr and Gunnlöd and Grídr, Mother-in-law of Nanna, Lady of the Æsir and Ásynjur, Mistress of Fulla and of the Hawk-Plumage and of Fensalir.

on.s: Hvernig skal Freyju kenna? Svá, at kalla hana dóttur Njarðar, systur Freys, konu Óðs, móður Hnossar, eigandi valfalls ok Sessrúmnis ok fressa, Brisíngamens, Vanagoð, Vanadís, it grátfagra goð, ástaguð. - Svá má kenna allar ásynjur at nefna annarrar nafni ok kenna við eign eða verk sín eða ættir.

is.s: Hvernig skal Freyju kenna? Svo, að kalla hana dóttur Njarðar, systur Freys, konu Óðs, móður Hnossar, eigandi valfalls og Sessrúmnis og fressa, Brisíngamens, Vanagoð, Vanadís, it grátfagra guð, ástaguð. - Svo má kenna allar ásynjur að nefna annarrar nafni og kenna við eign eða verk sín eða ættir.

en.s: "How should one periphrase Freyja? Thus: by calling her Daughter of Njördr, Sister of Freyr, Wife of Ódr, Mother of Hnoss, Possessor of the Slain, of Sessrúmnir, of the Gib-Cats, and of Brísinga-men; Goddess of the Vanir, Lady of the Vanir, Goddess Beautiful in Tears, Goddess of Love. All the goddesses may be periphrased thus: by calling them by the name of another, and naming them in terms of their possessions or their works or their kindred.

en-modern.s: "How should one periphrase Freyja? By calling her Daughter of Njördr, Sister of Freyr, Wife of Ódr, Mother of Hnoss, Possessor of the Slain, of Sessrúmnir, of the Tom-Cats and of Brísinga-men; Goddess of the Vanir, Lady of the Vanir, Goddess Beautiful in Tears, Goddess of Love. All the goddesses may be periphrased in this way: by calling each by the name of another, and naming them in terms of their possessions, their deeds or their family.

en.s: "How should Idunn be periphrased? Thus: by calling her Wife of Bragi, and Keeper of the Apples; and the apples should be called Age-Elixir of the Æsir. Idunn is also called Spoil of the Giant Thjazi, according to the tale that has been told before, how he took her away from the Æsir.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna manninn? Mann skal kenna við verk sín, þat er hann veitir eða þiggr eða gerir. Hann má ok kenna til eignar sinnar, þeirar er hann á, ok svá ef hann gaf, svá ok við ættir þær, er hann kom af, svá þær, er frá honum kómu. Hvernig skal hann kenna við þessa hluti? Svá, at kalla hann vinnanda eða fremjanda fara sinna eða athafnar, víga eða sæfara eða veiða eða vápna eða skipa. Ok fyrir því at hann er reynir vápnanna ok viðr víganna, allt eitt ok vinnandi. Viðr heitir tré. Reynir heitir ok tré. Af þessum heitum hafa skáldin kallat manninn ask eða hlyn, lund eða öðrum viðarheitum karlkenndum ok kennt til víga eða skipa eða fjár. Mann er ok rétt at kenna til allra ásaheita. Kennt er ok við jötnaheiti, ok er þat flest háð eða lastmæli. Vel þykkir kennt til álfa.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna manninn? Mann skal kenna við verk sín, það er hann veitir eða þiggur eða gerir. Hann má og kenna til eignar sinnar, þeirrar er hann á, og svo ef hann gaf, svo og við ættir þær, er hann kom af, svo þær, er frá honum komu. Hvernig skal hann kenna við þessa hluti? Svo, að kalla hann vinnanda eða fremjanda fara sinna eða athafnar, víga eða sæfara eða veiða eða vápna eða skipa. Og fyrir því að hann er reynir vápnanna og viður víganna, allt eitt og vinnandi. Viður heitir tré. Reynir heitir og tré. Af þessum heitum hafa skáldin kallað manninn ask eða hlyn, lund eða öðrum viðarheitum karlkenndum og kennt til víga eða skipa eða fjár. Mann er og rétt að kenna til allra ásaheita. Kennt er og við jötnaheiti, og er það flest háð eða lastmæli. Vel þykir kennt til álfa.

en.s: "How should man be periphrased? By his works, by that which he gives or receives or does; he may also be periphrased in terms of his property, those things which he possesses, and, if he be liberal, of his liberality; likewise in terms of the families from which he descended, as well as of those which have sprung from him. How is one to periphrase him in terms of these things? Thus, by calling him accomplisher or performer of his goings or his conduct, of his battles or sea-voyages or huntings or weapons or ships. And because he is a tester of weapons and a winner of battles,--the words for 'winner' and 'wood' being the same, as are also those for tester' and 'rowan,'--therefore, from these phrases, skalds have called man Ash or Maple, Grove, or other masculine tree-names, and periphrased him in such expressions in terms of battles or ships or possessions. It is also correct to periphrase man with all the names of the Æsir; also with giant-terms, and this last is for the most part for mocking or libellous purposes. Periphrasis with the names of elves is held to be favorable.

"Woman should be periphrased with reference to all female garments, gold and jewels, ale or wine or any other drink, or to that which she dispenses or gives; likewise with reference to ale-vessels, and to all those things which it becomes her to perform or to give.

en-modern.s: "How should man be periphrased? By his works, by what he gives or receives or does. He may also be periphrased in terms of his property, the things he owns, and, if he is generous, of his generosity; likewise in terms of the families he is descended from, as well as those that are descended from him. How is he to be periphrased in terms of these things? By calling him the accomplisher or performer of his journeys or his conduct, of his battles or sea voyages or hunts or weapons or ships. And because he is a tester of weapons and a winner of battles (the words for 'winner' and 'wood' being the same, as are those for 'tester' and 'rowan'), poets have, from these phrases, called man Ash or Maple, Grove, or other masculine tree-names, and periphrased him in such expressions in terms of battles or ships or possessions. It is also correct to periphrase man with all the names of the Æsir; also with giant-terms, and this is mostly for mockery or slander. Periphrasis with the names of elves is thought favourable.

"Woman should be periphrased with reference to all women's clothing, gold and jewels, ale or wine or any other drink, or to what she serves or gives; likewise with reference to ale-vessels, and to all the things that it is fitting for her to do or to give.

on.s: Konu skal kenna til alls kvenbúnaðar, gulls ok gimsteina, öls eða víns eða annars drykkjar, þess er hon selr eða gefr, svá ok til ölgagna ok allra þeira hluta, er henni samir at vinna eða veita. Rétt er at kenna hana svá at kalla hana selju eða lág þess, er hon miðlar, en selja eða lág, þat eru tré. Fyrir því er kona kölluð til kenningar öllum kvenkenndum viðarheitum. En fyrir því er kona kennd til gimsteina eða glersteina, at þat var í forneskju kvinnabúnaðr, er kallat var steinasörvi, er þær höfðu á hálsi sér. Nú er svá fært til kenningar, at konan er nú kennd við stein ok við öll steinsheiti. Kona er ok kennd við allar ásynjur eða valkyrjur eða nornir eða dísir. Konu er ok rétt at kenna við alla athöfn sína eða við eign eða ætt.

is.s: Konu skal kenna til alls kvenbúnaðar, gulls og gimsteina, öls eða víns eða annars drykkjar, þess er hún selur eða gefur, svo og til ölgagna og allra þeirra hluta, er henni samir að vinna eða veita. Rétt er að kenna hana svo að kalla hana selju eða lág þess, er hún miðlar, en selja eða lág, það eru tré. Fyrir því er kona kölluð til kenningar öllum kvenkenndum viðarheitum. En fyrir því er kona kennd til gimsteina eða glersteina, að það var í forneskju kvinnabúnaður, er kallað var steinasörvi, er þær höfðu á hálsi sér. Nú er svo fært til kenningar, að konan er nú kennd við stein og við öll steinsheiti. Kona er og kennd við allar ásynjur eða valkyrjur eða nornir eða dísir. Konu er og rétt að kenna við alla athöfn sína eða við eign eða ætt.

en.s: It is correct to periphrase her thus: by calling her giver or user of that of which she partakes. But the words for 'giver' and 'user' are also names of trees; therefore woman is called in metaphorical speech by all feminine tree-names. Woman is periphrased with reference to jewels or agates for this reason: in heathen times what was called a 'stone-necklace,' which they wore about the neck, was a part of a woman's apparel; now it is used figuratively in such a way as to periphrase woman with stones and all names of stones. Woman is also metaphorically called by the names of the Ásynjur or the Valkyrs or Norris or women of supernatural kind. It is also correct to periphrase woman in terms of all her conduct or property or family.

on.s: Hvernig skal kenna gull? Svá, at kalla þat eld Ægis ok barr Glasis, haddr Sifjar, höfuðband Fullu, grátr Freyju, munntal ok rödd ok orð jötna, dropa Draupnis ok regn eða skúr Draupnis eða augna Freyju, otrgjöld, nauðgjald ásanna, sáð Fýrisvalla, haugþak Hölga, eldr allra vatna ok handar, grjót ok sker eða blik handar.

is.s: Hvernig skal kenna gull? Svo, að kalla það eld Ægis og barr Glasis, haddur Sifjar, höfuðband Fullu, grátur Freyju, munntal og rödd og orð jötna, dropa Draupnis og regn eða skúr Draupnis eða augna Freyju, otrgjöld, nauðgjald ásanna, sáð Fýrisvalla, haugþak Hölga, eldur allra vatna og handar, grjót og sker eða blik handar.

en.s: "How should gold be periphrased? Thus: by calling it Ægir's Fire, and Needles of Glasir, Hair of Sif, Snood of Fulla, Freyja's Tears, Talk and Voice and Word of Giants, Draupnir's Drop and Rain or Shower of Draupnir, or of Freyja's Eyes, Otter's Ransom, Forced Payment of the Æsir, Seed of Fýris-Plain, Cairn-Roof of Hölgi, Fire of all Waters and of the Hand, Stone and Reef or Gleam of the Hand.

on.s: Fyrir hví er gull kallat eldr Ægis? Þessi saga er til þess, er fyrr er getit, at Ægir sótti heimboð til Ásgarðs, en er hann var búinn til heimferðar, þá bauð hann til sín Óðni ok öllum ásum á þriggja mánaða fresti. Til þeirar ferðar varð fyrst Óðinn ok Njörðr, Freyr, Týr, Bragi, Viðarr, Loki, svá ok ásynjur Frigg, Freyja, Gefjun, Skaði, Iðunn, Sif. Þórr var eigi þar. Hann var farinn í austrveg at drepa troll. En er goðin höfðu setzt í sæti, þá lét Ægir bera inn á hallargólf lýsigull, þat er birti ok lýsti höllina sem eldr, ok þat var þar haft fyrir ljós at hans veizlu, sem í Valhöllu váru sverðin fyrir eld. Þá sennti Loki þar við öll goð ok drap þræl Ægis, þann er Fimafengr hét. Annarr þræll hans er nefndr Eldir. Rán er nefnd kona hans, en níu dætr þeira, svá sem fyrr er ritat. At þeiri veizlu vannst allt sjálft, bæði vist ok öl ok öll reiða, er til veizlunnar þurfti. Þá urðu æsir þessir varir, at Rán átti net þat, er hon veiddi í menn alla, þá er á sæ kómu.

is.s: Fyrir hví er gull kallað eldur Ægis? Þessi saga er til þess, er fyrr er getið, að Ægir sótti heimboð til Ásgarðs, en er hann var búinn til heimferðar, þá bauð hann til sín Óðni og öllum ásum á þriggja mánaða fresti. Til þeirrar ferðar varð fyrst Óðinn og Njörður, Freyr, Týr, Bragi, Viðar, Loki, svo og ásynjur Frigg, Freyja, Gefjun, Skaði, Iðunn, Sif. Þór var eigi þar. Hann var farinn í austurveg að drepa troll. En er goðin höfðu sest í sæti, þá lét Ægir bera hinn á hallargólf lýsigull, það er birti og lýsti höllina sem eldur, og það var þar haft fyrir ljós að hans veizlu, sem í Valhöllu voru sverðin fyrir eld. Þá sennti Loki þar við öll guð og drap þræl Ægis, þann er Fimafengur hét. Annar þræll hans er nefndur Eldir. Ron er nefnd kona hans, en níu dætur þeirra, svo sem fyrr er ritað. Að þeirri veizlu vannst allt sjálft, bæði vist og öl og öll reiða, er til veizlunnar þurfti. Þá urðu æsir þessir varir, að Ron átti net það, er hún veiddi í menn alla, þá er á sæ komu.

en.s: Wherefore is gold called Ægir's Fire? This tale is to the same purport as we have told before: Ægir went to Ásgard to a feast, but when he was ready to return home, he invited Odin and all the Æsir to visit him in three months' time. First came Odin and Njördr, Freyr, Týr, Bragi, Vídarr, Loki; likewise the Ásynjur: Frigg, Freyja, Gefjun, Skadi, Idunn, Sif. Thor was not there, having gone into the eastern lands to slay trolls. When the gods had sat down in their places, straightway Ægir had bright gold brought in onto the floor of the hall, and the gold gave forth light and illumined the hall like fire: and it was used there for lights at his banquet, even as in Valhall swords were used in place of fire. Then Loki bandied sharp words with all the gods, and slew one of Ægir's thralls, him who was called Five-Finger; another of his thralls was named Fire-Kindler. Rán is the name of Ægir's wife, and their daughters are nine, even as we have written before. At this feast all things were self-served, both food and ale, and all implements needful to the feast. Then the Æsir became aware that Rán had that net wherein she was wont to catch all men who go upon the sea.

en-modern.s: Why is gold called Ægir's Fire? This story is to the same effect as the one we told before: Ægir went to a feast in Ásgard, and when he was ready to go home he invited Odin and all the Æsir to visit him in three months' time. First came Odin and Njördr, Freyr, Týr, Bragi, Vídarr, Loki; likewise the Ásynjur: Frigg, Freyja, Gefjun, Skadi, Idunn, Sif. Thor was not there, as he had gone into the eastern lands to kill trolls. When the gods had sat down in their places, Ægir at once had bright gold brought in onto the floor of the hall, and the gold gave out light and lit up the hall like fire; it was used there for light at his banquet, just as in Valhall swords were used in place of fire. Then Loki traded sharp words with all the gods, and killed one of Ægir's slaves, the one called Five-Finger; another of his slaves was called Fire-Kindler. Rán is the name of Ægir's wife, and they have nine daughters, as we have written before. At this feast everything served itself, both food and ale, and all the utensils the feast needed. Then the Æsir discovered that Rán had the net in which she used to catch all men who go to sea.

on.s: Nú er þessi saga til þess, hvaðan af þat er, at gull er kallat eldr eða ljós eða birti Ægis, Ránar eða Ægis dætra. Ok af þeim kenningum er nú svá sett, at gull er kallat eldr sævar ok allra hans heita, svá sem Ægir eða Rán eigu heiti við sæinn, ok þaðan af er nú gull kallat eldr vatna eða á ok allra árheita. En þessi heiti hafa svá farit sem önnur ok kenningar, at in yngri skáld hafa ort eftir dæmum inna gömlu skálda, svá sem stóð í þeira kvæðum, en sett síðan út í hálfur þær, er þeim þóttu líkar við þat, er fyrr var ort, svá sem vatnit er sænum, en áin vatninu, en bekkr ánni. Því er þat kallat nýgervingar allt, er út er sett heiti lengra en fyrr finnst, ok þykkir þat vel allt, er með líkendum ferr ok eðli. Svá kvað Bragi skáld:

is.s: Nú er þessi saga til þess, hvaðan af það er, að gull er kallað eldur eða ljós eða birti Ægis, Ránar eða Ægis dætra. Og af þeim kenningum er nú svo sett, að gull er kallað eldur sævar og allra hans heita, svo sem Ægir eða Ron eiga heiti við sæinn, og þaðan af er nú gull kallað eldur vatna eða á og allra árheita. En þessi heiti hafa svo farið sem önnur og kenningar, að hin yngri skáld hafa ort eftir dæmum inna gömlu skálda, svo sem stóð í þeirra kvæðum, en sett síðan út í hálfur þær, er þeim þóttu líkar við það, er fyrr var ort, svo sem vatnið er sænum, en áin vatninu, en bekkur ánni. Því er það kallað nýgervingar allt, er út er sett heiti lengra en fyrr finnst, og þykir það vel allt, er með líkindum fer og eðli. Svo kvað Bragi skáld:

en.s: Now this tale is to show whence it comes that gold is called Fire or Light or Brightness of Ægir, of Rán, or of Ægir's daughters; and now such use is made of these metaphors that gold is called Fire of the Sea, and of all names of the sea, even as Ægir or Rán had names associated with the sea. Therefore gold is now called Fire of Waters or of Rivers, and of all river names.

"But these names have fared just as other figures also have done: the later skalds have composed after the examples of the old skalds, even those examples which stood in their poems, but were later expanded into such forms as seemed to later poets to be like what was written before: as a lake is to the sea, or the river to the lake, or the brook to the river. Therefore all these are called new figures, when terms are expanded to greater length than what was recorded before; and all this seems well and good, so fair as it concurs with verisimilitude and nature. As Bragi the Skald sang:

So gold is now called Fire of Waters or of Rivers, and of all river names.

So all these are called new figures, when terms are expanded to greater length than what was recorded before; and all this seems well and good, so far as it agrees with likelihood and nature.
